THE  COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 -2-  NC: 2024:KHC-D:7970  CRL.P No. 101120 of 2024  ORDER Heard Sri. Vidyashankar G. Dalawai, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri. Praveena Y.
Devareddiyavara, learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1-State.

Sri. Ganapati M. Bhat, learned counsel for respondent No.2.
2.

The petitioner is before this Court seeking regular bail in Crime No.65/2023 of respondent Police Station, for the offences punishable under Sections 363, 376(3) of IPC and Sections 6, 8 and 12 of POCSO Act, 2012.
3. It is the case of the prosecution that the complainant is working as an Advocate.
He was staying along with his wife and daughter.
His daughter was aged about 15 years 11 months and she was studying in Akshara English Medium School.
When she was studying in the said school, she acquainted with the petitioner and exchanged their phone numbers and talking with each other.
After coming to know the said fact, the complainant sent his daughter to the house of her aunt situated at Bengaluru.
Thereafter, the victim developed stomach ache and she was taken to Victoria hospital, Bengaluru for medical check up.
There, it is diagnosed that the victim was pregnant.
And the said pregnancy reached upto one and half month.

5. It is further submitted that after hearing the said news, when it was questioned to the victim, the complainant informed that victim had been subjected to sexual assault on 13.09.2023 around 5.00 p.m. and thereafter, she was threatened that she should not disclose it to anybody.
The complainant after having received the information from the victim, informed the police.
The police have registered a case in Crime No.65/2023.
After conducting investigation, submitted the charge sheet.
6. It is the submission of the learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner is innocent of the alleged offence.
He has not committed any offence as alleged NC: 2024:KHC-D:7970 against him.
The DNA report in respect of the paternity has not been obtained and it is not placed along with the charge sheet.
The statement of prosecutrix cannot be construed as conclusive proof in respect of the alleged sexual assault.

2 7.

It is further submitted that the petitioner is aged about 22 years and working at Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) and permanent resident of Harihara, Halladkeri Circle and he will abide the conditions imposed by this Court in the event of his release on bail.
Making such submission, the learned counsel for the petitioner prays to allow the petition.

8. Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader vehemently opposed the bail petition and submitted that the victim narrated the incident to her parents and it has been diagnosed that the victim was pregnant.
Since, the petitioner has committed heinous offence, it is not appropriate to grant him bail.
Making such submission, the learned HCGP prays to dismiss the petition.

Having heard the learned counsel for the respective parties and also perused the averments of the charge sheet as well as the complaint, it appears from the record that the petitioner had visited the school where the victim was studying on the NGO work.
Both acquainted with each other and exchanged their phone numbers and they were loving each other.
10. It is alleged that victim has been raped by the petitioner and she became pregnant.
Having considered the age of the victim and also gravity and nature of the offence.
I am of the considered opinion that, it is not a fit case to grant bail.

11. Hence, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition is rejected.
